newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian oil firm seeks $100 mln syndicated loan.
newsitem.headline: Croatian oil firm seeks $100 mln syndicated loan.

text.p: Croatian national oil group INA Industrija Nafte d.d. said on Wednesday it soon planned to raise $100 million through a syndicated loan facility.
"The funds will be used to improve INA's business and to refinance some of the old loans taken at less favourable terms," president Andrija Kojakovic told a news conference.
The lead arranger is Bankers Trust International and five leading international banks would be co-arrangers, he said.
Final terms are to be announced later this week in London.
It will be the first loan to INA without government guarantee, and that Kojakovic said reflected increased creditor confidence in a "new INA".

The company was partly restructured when the government took over its considerable foreign liabilities dating back to the former Yugoslav times. The move went hand in hand with the overhaul of its main creditor Privredna Banka.
In exchange the group handed over holdings in some of its non-core businesses and also shed other subsidiaries.
"We are still at the beginning of true business restructuring, which will be completed with a listing on the London Stock Exchange in 1999," Kojakovic said.
He mentioned among development projects, for which INA may have to seek some external backing, upgrading of refineries and natural gas exploration in the northern Adriatic.
Developing of refining facilities could cost the company $100 million over the next five years, company officials said.
In 1996 it spent 317 million kuna ($52.4 million) on this.
INA expects to post a group pre-tax profit in the region of 250 million kuna this year.
Its production plans total 1.7 million tonnes of crude and 4.8 million tonnes of oil derivatives. Natural gas output is pencilled in at 1.8 billion cubic metres.
The group made a net loss of 1.2 billion kuna in 1995 and no figures are as yet available for last year's performance. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075 ($ = 6.054 Croatian Kuna)
